title: Despotate of Dobruja
capsule: The Despotate of Dobruja was a semi-independent Bulgarian polity in the region between the lower Danube and the Black Sea coast (modern Romania and Bulgaria), established around 1360 by Despot Dobrotitsa after the fragmentation of the Second Bulgarian Empire. Dobrotitsa maintained a substantial Black Sea fleet, concluded treaties with Genoa and Ragusa, and contested Ottoman expansion into the Balkans. His son Ivanko inherited the despotate but capitulated to Ottoman pressure; by 1396, following the Battle of Nicopolis, the region was absorbed into the Ottoman Empire. The despotate represents a last flash of autonomous Bulgarian political life on the Pontic steppe frontier before five centuries of Ottoman rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory is reasonably defined by the natural borders of the Danube and Black Sea, but the precise northern and western limits of Dobrotitsa's effective control are incompletely mapped in surviving sources.
